column3: “Assyria” follows the Hebrew; some suggest “a cypress.” “Between branches” is rendered “among the clouds.”
“Going around” is rendered “continually extended all around.”
“As it sprouted” is NASB’s phrasing; the Hebrew “in sending it out” is difficult.
“Eclipsed” is rendered “could not match,” and “fir trees” as “cypresses.”
“You were tall” is rendered “it is high,” and “between branches” as “among the clouds.”
“A leader of nations” is rendered “a despot,” and “I drove it out” as “I have driven it.”
“Their mighty ones” follows a difficult phrase; NASB has “well-watered mighty ones.”
“Covered over” is rendered “closed,” and “caused mourning” as “caused lamentations.”
“Its arm” is rendered “those who were its strength.”
“Earth of the lower parts” is rendered “earth beneath.”
